- On March 18, 2022, Fortune Brands Home & Security, Inc., a Delaware corporation, executed a Second Amendment and Incremental Agreement to obtain an additional $500,000,000 incremental term loan under their existing 364-Day Term Loan Credit Agreement originally dated November 29, 2021.
- The borrower is Fortune Brands Home & Security, Inc., operating in the home and security products sector. The transaction involves JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent, with incremental lenders including JPMorgan Chase Bank, Credit Suisse AG (New York Branch), and Bank of America, N.A.
- This incremental facility increases the total term loan commitment to $1.1 billion, with proceeds designated for general corporate purposes including working capital, capital expenditures, permitted acquisitions, and other lawful corporate purposes.
- The company maintains an established banking relationship with premier financial institutions, having previously accessed $400 million in initial term loans and a $200 million first amendment incremental loan.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
• Strong banking consortium including JPMorgan Chase Bank, Bank of America, and Credit Suisse, indicating continued lender confidence and relationship strength
• Successful track record of accessing incremental facilities, demonstrating market acceptance and credit quality
• Flexible use of proceeds allows management discretion for growth initiatives, working capital optimization, and strategic acquisitions
• Borrower remains in full compliance with all existing covenants and representations, with no defaults occurring
• Terms of the incremental loan are identical to existing term loans, suggesting consistent credit profile

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• Significant leverage increase with $500 million additional debt on top of $600 million existing term loans, raising total debt to $1.1 billion
• 364-day term structure creates near-term refinancing risk requiring successful renewal or alternative financing
• Limited covenant detail available in the amendment restricts comprehensive credit assessment
• General corporate purposes provide broad use flexibility but may indicate less specific strategic rationale
